source: Leveson & Turner, 'An Investigation of the Therac-25 Accidents', IEEE Computer 1993
summary: A radiation therapy machine (1985-87) delivered massive overdoses. No single broken part: a concurrency race between the operator-input task and the setup task, hardware interlocks removed (software 'replaced' them), code reused from the Therac-20 whose bugs were masked by hardware there, and fast operator editing combined to command a high-energy beam while the turntable was in field-light position.

next_actions: name losses (L: patient harmed by radiation)
name system-level hazards

lean_mapping.obligation: define the bad predicate the whole analysis targets
lean_mapping.lean: def hazard (s : State) : Prop := s.deliveredDose > s.prescribedDose * safetyFactor

steps.outcome: hazard predicate fixed → everything downstream refers to it

rules.S3: define hazard as a system state

next_actions: add each controller & controlled process
check every loop has feedback

lean_mapping.obligation: control graph well-formed; every control loop has feedback
lean_mapping.lean: theorem wf : ∀ l ∈ loops, feedback l ≠ none   -- FAILS at beam→software

steps.outcome: missing feedback flagged (software cannot observe actual turntable state) → prime suspect

short.move: who commands whom — and the missing feedback

rules.S2: let the operator see actual machine state

next_actions: list control actions: set-energy, set-filter, fire-beam

lean_mapping.obligation: enumerate the transition labels (actions) of the state machine

steps.outcome: action set fixed → cross with guidewords next

rules.S2: preserve a way to catch a mis-set energy
rules.S3: bound beam energy by verified setup

steps.state: each action × {not given / given / wrong timing / wrong order}
next_actions: given wrong value: high energy w/ field-light filter
wrong order: fire before filter set
wrong timing: edit after setup latched
steps.chosen: UCA1 = fire high-energy beam while turntable in field-light position

lean_mapping.obligation: grid coverage (∀ action, a verdict) AND each UCA names a bad state (non-vacuity)
lean_mapping.lean:
def UCA1 (s) := s.turntable = fieldLight ∧ s.energy = high ∧ s.firing
 theorem uca1_bad : UCA1 s → hazard s

steps.outcome: UCA1 (and siblings) identified → become safety constraints

rules.S1: don't fire high energy in field-light (procedure)
rules.S3: interlock blocks high energy unless flattener in place

next_actions: state the invariant C1
classify: provable statically or must be monitored?
steps.chosen: C1 = never fire high energy unless turntable confirmed in beam-flattener position

lean_mapping.obligation: the constraint excludes the UCA state
lean_mapping.lean:
def C1 (s) := s.firing ∧ s.energy = high → s.turntable = flattener
 theorem c1_excludes : C1 s → ¬ UCA1 s

steps.outcome: C1 is the property whose violation the accident will show

rules.S2: keep time/feedback to catch the race
rules.S3: fire high energy only if turntable=flattener (monitor)

steps.stage: 4b · why would C1 be violated? (causal factors)
steps.state: trace how the controller could issue the unsafe action
next_actions: flawed process model (SW believes turntable set)
unsafe feedback (no position sensor read)
concurrency: edit races setup task
steps.chosen: software's process model diverges from reality via a race

lean_mapping.obligation: model the controller's belief vs actual; C1 proof needs the belief to track reality
lean_mapping.lean:
theorem c1_needs_feedback : (s.belief.turntable = s.turntable) → C1 s
  -- discharges ONLY under the (false) feedback assumption

steps.outcome: root factor: C1 provable only if belief=reality, which the missing feedback + race breaks

short.move: belief ≠ reality: a race, no sensor
short.out: holds only if software sees truth

rules.S2: fast edits happen — design for them
rules.S3: never trust software belief without a sensor

next_actions: construct trace: select X-ray, edit to electron within 8s, setup task already latched
check which invariant it violates
steps.chosen: trace reaches firing with energy=high ∧ turntable=fieldLight

lean_mapping.obligation: the trace is a genuine counterexample to a named invariant
lean_mapping.lean: theorem accident : ∃ t, reach t ∧ ¬ C1 (state t)   -- CAST = the witness trace

steps.outcome: accident = constructive ¬C1; this is exactly a model-checker counterexample

rules.S2: no feedback to catch the race

steps.state: why each higher controller allowed it
next_actions: AECL: reused Therac-20 code, inadequate test of concurrency
regulator: no requirement for independent interlock
safety culture: trusted software over hardware interlock
steps.chosen: interlocks removed in favor of software; reuse masked by old hardware

lean_mapping.obligation: the assumption set the proof rests on is explicit and owned
lean_mapping.lean:
axiom feedback_present : ∀ s, s.belief.turntable = s.turntable
  -- the UNJUSTIFIED assumption; CAST attributes it up the hierarchy

steps.outcome: the false axiom is the organizational cause, made explicit as a named assumption

short.move: reused code · interlocks removed · no reg check

rules.S1: trusted software over the hardware interlock
rules.S2: removed the margin the hardware gave

steps.state: choose how to make C1 hold
next_actions: add position feedback (restore the real sensor)
hardware interlock (monitor enforces C1)
prove belief=reality given the new feedback
steps.chosen: independent hardware interlock = runtime monitor of C1

lean_mapping.obligation: a monitor enforces a safety property (Schneider: safety ⇒ enforceable)
lean_mapping.lean: theorem monitor_sound : ∀ s, guard s = allow → C1 s

steps.outcome: C1 now holds by construction; UCA1 unreachable

steps.state: ops asks: can we drop the interlock to speed throughput?
next_actions: propose C1' (weaker)
require certificate: does H still hold?
accept iff provable, else refuse with the hazard
steps.chosen: refuse: no certificate that hazard-free holds without the interlock

lean_mapping.obligation: loosening admissible iff weakened constraint still entails the hazard invariant
lean_mapping.lean:
-- SAFE iff provable:  theorem loosen_ok : C1' s → ¬ hazard s
-- here UNPROVABLE → loosening refused (the exact pre-accident mistake)

steps.outcome: the tool blocks the 1980s decision; shows the re-enabled accident. Ratchet is on H, not on C1.

short.move: drop the interlock for speed? prove H first

rules.S1: relax checks only if still safe
rules.S2: don't drop the interlock for speed
rules.S3: refuse unless H provable without the interlock
